Both frameworks pick a render mode per route with one export in the route file. SSR: Zero export const renderMode = 'ssr', Next.js export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. SSG: renderMode = 'ssg' against dynamic = 'force-static'. ISR: renderMode = 'isr' against revalidate = 60. Zero also has a per-route 'spa' mode, routeRules globs that set modes in one place, and mode: 'auto' (experimental), which infers each route's mode and prints the table at build.

Two stacks. React Native: your JavaScript bundle runs on the phone in the Hermes JavaScript engine, and React Native's renderer drives the platform widgets. Pyreon: your .tsx is compiled on your machine by PMTC into SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose source, Xcode and Gradle build a native binary, and the phone runs SwiftUI and Compose views with no JavaScript engine under the UI. The Pyreon native targets are labelled experimental.

AI and MCP documentation: An MCP server with 24 tools: your assistant looks up the real API, validates its code against Pyreon's misuse detectors and explains reactivity. No network calls.

Storage documentation: Signals that persist: localStorage synced across tabs, sessionStorage, cookies the server can read, and IndexedDB, all behind one API.
